core_obligations: Compare the two topologies in one direction (proof lines 4883-4886): with F^n = ker(M -> H^p(C, F_n)), observe IF^n is contained in F^{n+1}, hence I^n M is contained in F^n, so the I-adic topology is finer than the limit topology.

Produce the graded input (proof lines 4890-4911): the injective maps F^n/F^{n+1} -> H^p(C, F_{n+1}) land in the image of H^p(C, I^n F_{n+1}), whose inverse images E_n form a graded submodule of the direct sum of the H^p(C, I^n F_{n+1}); the chain condition makes that submodule finitely generated, hence so is the direct sum of the F^n/F^{n+1}, giving elements a_i in F^{c_i} generating it and c = max(c_i).

Prove the key identity (proof lines 4914-4925): for n >= c show IF^n = F^{n+1} by writing an element of F^{n+1} as a combination of the a_i modulo F^{n+2}, then splitting the coefficients through I; a simple induction gives F^{n+1} = F^{n+e} + IF^n for all e > 0, so IF^n is dense in F^{n+1}.

Apply the open mapping lemma (proof lines 4926-4937): for generators k_1, ..., k_r of I the map u : (F^n)^{direct sum r} -> F^{n+1} has dense image on each (F^m)^{direct sum r}, so the open mapping lemma makes u open and hence surjective, giving IF^n = F^{n+1} for n >= c and therefore F^{n+c} = I^n F^c contained in I^n M.
proof_roadmap: Introduce the neighbourhoods F^n of the limit topology and note I^n M is contained in F^n.
Use the chain condition to get finitely many graded generators of the F^n/F^{n+1}.
Show IF^n = F^{n+1} for large n by the coefficient splitting and an induction.
Upgrade density of IF^n in F^{n+1} to equality using the open mapping lemma.
Conclude that the limit topology is no finer than the I-adic topology, hence they agree.
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares two topologies on M = lim H^p(C, F_n): the limit topology and the I-adic topology, showing they agree under an ascending chain condition on the graded module of the H^p(C, I^n F_{n+1}) (statement lines 4864-4880). The proof has three genuinely different ingredients: the containment I^n M contained in F^n giving one inclusion of topologies, the graded finite generation produced by the chain condition which supplies elements a_i that control F^n/F^{n+1} (proof lines 4890-4911), and the passage from density of IF^n in F^{n+1} to equality via the open mapping lemma applied to the map u : (F^n)^{direct sum r} -> F^{n+1} built from generators of I (proof lines 4914-4937). The claim is H2: a multi-step topological argument whose hardest step is the open mapping application.
